title: Papoose's funeral and the serenaders Walter, Sam and Noon
summary: The son of Walter, a guitarist, died of an overdose; his funeral band stopped four hours at a joint.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, that's what happened. The people of the day, I don't care, right now, you let a band pass out, right out there, we don't know nothing's going on. And you'll see people coming from all directions. The last time they had a funeral from down here, this boy, he played with, you mean Papoose? Yeah, he played with Fat Dominic. He died in California. Or New York, I think it was. He died in New York. Well his daddy, called Walter, he played the guitar out there as well. Now Slowdrag, him, Noon, well they used to go around and play together. But mostly Walter, Sam, and Noon. Noon made his own, Noon made his own, and they used to go around and serenade in different places, all around the French Quarter. But I don't know, those fellas like they get, they're trifling. Now Walter, his son played music, his wife played music, his daughters, his sisters play music, all them play guitar. He played music, and he played music. That little boy was a wonderful thing. He got in that dope racket, that's what happened to him. That overdose, that killed him. Well when they buried him, the Caledonia, well the Caledonia, the front of the Caledonia furnished the music. They didn't have nobody out but the second line in the band. So I said to the fellas, I said, well why is it members? It ain't no Caledonia, which I know it's no Caledonia. I said, ain't no members. I said, look at the members out there with the umbrella. And they goes down there, and the next block, on the next Long Street, where Delio used to be, I forgot to call the girls' name, Ogapiku, that's what joint. And them people stayed in there about four hours. And our men, you wouldn't have walked, it wasn't carnival they, down that block. They went in that place, the band went inside and they stayed in there. And they were like, well a lot of the time we have a funeral and then we wind up back at the Tulane Club, we go back in the hall and join them. They played four or five members for them. And my wife now loaded down. Yeah, it goes.
